amendments.rule: The conjunction `וְ` is normally English *and*, including the waw of a consecutive verb form: the conjunction takes *And* and the verb takes the verb. Where the ASV renders it by some other connective, align it to that word instead. **The list is open and is read off the ASV rather than checked against a set**: the corpus already aligns a waw to *but*, *then*, *so*, *or*, *now*, *also*, *for*, *therefore*, *neither*, *nor*, *yea*, *yet*, *even*, *with*, *moreover* and *howbeit*, among others. A connective the ASV has written for a waw is never `added`, and it is never folded into a neighbouring word to avoid one: a town list writes *with* for the waw of `וְחַצְרֵיהֶן` → *with their villages* and *even* for the waw of `וָיָמָּה` → *even unto the sea*, and each waw takes the word written for it. **Where the ASV renders one waw by a correlative pair such as *both … and* or *either … or*, both English words belong to the waw's one discontinuous unit, headed on the closing connective (*and* or *or*); the opening correlative is not `added`.** **But that governs only a pair no other morpheme has a claim on.** Where another morpheme standing in the clause is itself what the opening correlative says — a present negative for the *neither* of *neither … nor*, the `מִן` of a `מִן … עַד` range for the *both* of *both … and* — that morpheme takes the opening word and the waw takes only the closing connective, exactly as rule 47 gives a written *the* to a present article before a supplied one and rule 46 gives a *that* to a present relative before a bare participle. `אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יָדְעוּ הֵמָּה וַאֲבוֹתָם` → *whom* ***neither*** *they* ***nor*** *their fathers have known* gives *neither* to `לֹא` and *nor* to the waw, and `מֵעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָה` → ***both*** *the birds of the heavens* ***and*** *the beasts* gives *both* to `מִן` and *and* to the waw, leaving the `עַד` `unrepresented` under rule 40. Count the correlative's members against the morphemes that could carry them, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s. This does not touch rule 35's fusion, which is a single English word carrying every morpheme's sense: a lone *Nor* or *neither* with no answering *nor* written is that rule's, and only a written pair is this one's. Read what stands in the clause for that waw in particular, as rule 51 requires for *also*, and where the ASV leaves it unrendered, mark it `unrepresented`. **But read whether a waw is present at all before placing the connective.** Where the ASV writes a coordinating *and*, *or* or *but* for a clause or phrase in which no conjunction morpheme stands, no morpheme licenses that word and it is its own `added` unit under rule 30. Hebrew juxtaposes where English coordinates, and the ASV supplies the connective freely: `עַל־כָּתֵף תִּשָּׂא בָּעֲלָטָה תוֹצִיא` → *shalt thou bear it upon thy shoulder,* ***and*** *carry it forth in the dark* writes one for a clause the Hebrew leaves asyndetic, and `לְיוֹשְׁבֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם אֶל־אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל` → *concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem* ***and*** *the land of Israel* writes one for a second prepositional phrase the Hebrew merely sets beside the first. Do not fold such a word into the preposition, the verb or the noun standing next to it to avoid the `added`, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and* and rule 51 about a supplied *also*: the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them, and a preposition whose own relation the ASV has left unstated is `unrepresented` under rule 40 rather than a home for a coordinator. Count the clause's conjunctions against the ASV's connectives, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s, and mark whichever side is in surplus. Read the clause before counting, since a morpheme that has an English word of its own is not made a surplus by this sentence: a present negative carries a *nor* or a *neither* under rule 35, a `כִּי` or an `אִם` carries a *but* or an *or* the ASV has written for it, and only a connective no morpheme answers to is `added`. **And a coordinator standing inside one morpheme's own English rendering is not a connective supplied for the clause at all.** Where the ASV renders a single source morpheme by a fixed English phrase that contains an *and* or an *or*, the word coordinates the parts of that phrase and not two source items, so it belongs to that morpheme's unit, is neither `added` nor a separate connective, and does not move the unit's head, which rule 44 leaves on the lexical verb because a phrasal particle names nothing on its own. Decide it by asking what stands on either side of the English word in the Hebrew, which is the subtraction test rules 16, 31 and 43 use and the one rule 30 applies to its one-English-word condition. Where a source clause or phrase stands on each side, the preceding sentences govern and a connective no waw answers to is `added`; where the same one morpheme's rendering runs on both sides and no source item is coordinated at all, the word is written inside that rendering rather than beside it. `וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ בְּתוֹךְ אֲרָיוֹת` → *And he went up and down among the lions* keeps *up and down* whole with the one verb it renders, while `אָבְדָה תִקְוָתָהּ` → ***and*** *her hope was lost* leaves its supplied *and* `added`, because there a written clause stands on either side of it.
amendments.why: Rule 14's last paragraph was written for coordination between clauses and between prepositional phrases, and both of its examples are of that shape. EZK.19 met the case it had not considered. The chapter has exactly two supplied coordinators, both at 19:5, where a written Hebrew clause stands on each side of the English *and*, and both are correctly `added`; and one English *and* at 19:6, inside *went up and down* for the single Hithpael `וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ`, with no source item on either side of it to coordinate. Read literally, the existing sentence marks that second *and* `added` too, which would strip a word out of the middle of one morpheme's own English phrase — the same mistake rule 44 already forbids for the *up* and the *down* around it. It is an amendment rather than a new rule because a cross-reference would leave the over-broad sentence standing for whoever reads it first. The test written here is the contract's own subtraction test and is tight: it turns on what the Hebrew puts on either side of the English word, so it cannot be used to fold a genuine clause-level coordinator into a neighbouring verb, and the chapter's own two halves sit on opposite sides of it. Nothing in the supplied corpus contradicts it; those tables are keyed by source lemma and record no treatment of a coordinator internal to a verb's rendering either way.

conventions: The ASV's pronoun for a pronominal suffix repeatedly disagrees with that suffix in number or gender in this chapter, and the written pronoun is what is aligned in every case: `אַלְמְנוֹתָיו` → *their palaces*, `קוֹמָתוֹ` → *their stature*, `גָבְהוֹ` → *their height* and `דָּלִיֹּתָיו` → *their branches* all give a plural English possessive to a 3ms suffix, and `אֲכָלָתְהוּ` → *consumed them* gives a plural object pronoun to a 3ms object suffix. The ASV's own marginal *Hebrew his* and *Hebrew he was* notes at 19:11 mark exactly these places; they are translator's notes on the Hebrew, not a second rendering, and they neither move an edge nor license marking the suffix `unrepresented`. Align the pronoun the ASV wrote under rule 18 and let the margin stand.

report: Checked all 27 candidate lemmas. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in different clauses, and the source licenses each difference. The two loudest are not splits: `בְּתוֹךְ` is split at v.2 (*in the midst of*, separate words for each morpheme) and fused at v.6 (*among*, one English word), which is exactly rule 30's one-English-word condition, and both verses already say so; `עַל־בֵּין` at v.11 fuses to *among* while the bare `בֵּין` at v.2 takes *among* alone, because no `עַל` stands at v.2.

Read the dump for supplied connectives, which the table cannot see. The ASV writes a coordinating *and* for an asyndetic clause exactly twice in this chapter, both at v.5 (*and her hope was lost*, *and made him a young lion*), and both are `added` under rule 14's last paragraph. Every other asyndetic clause in the chapter — v.2, v.3 (`כְּפִיר הָיָה`, `אָדָם אָכָל`), v.4, v.8, v.9 (third `יְבִאֻהוּ`), v.12 (twice), v.14 (`אָכָלָה`) — is written with no English connective, so nothing is in surplus there. The chapter is internally consistent on this.

The one place an English *and* is neither `added` nor a waw's is v.6's *went up and down* for `וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ`, where the word stands inside one morpheme's own English phrase with no source item on either side of it. That is not the same construction as v.5's two supplied coordinators, and it is the case rule 14's last paragraph did not consider, so it is returned as an amendment to rule 14 rather than leaving the over-broad sentence in place.

BSB: the single listed disagreement, EZK.19.11 `לָ֞` (*to*), is a documented convention difference and not an error. `וַיִּהְיוּ לָהּ מַטּוֹת עֹז` → *And it had strong rods* is rule 43's clause verbatim — `הָיָה` is present, so it takes the *had*, the suffix takes the subject pronoun *it*, and the possessive `לְ` is left with no English word (rules 40, 43). BSB attaches the preposition to its phrase; that is its convention, and the accepted edge stands.

One judgment I looked at and left alone: v.14 gives *out* to `יָצָא` (*is gone out*) and *of* to `מִן`, where the corpus records 476 units of `מִן` → *out of* headed on *out*. Both readings are defensible, the verse note names the competing one under rule 8, and this is a single occurrence with no second instance in the chapter to be inconsistent with, so it is not a cross-verse split and I have not disturbed it. A corpus filter on `יָצָא` with `מִן` following would settle it for a later chapter; it would change nothing here.

Conventions: one recorded, on the ASV's number- and gender-mismatched pronouns for suffixes (v.7, v.11 ×3, v.12), which the ASV's own margins flag. The other 27 repeated notes in the validation report restate rules 15, 18, 19, 25, 29 and 44 and need no log entry.
